configuration-backup.goal: Restore original authoritative facts without inventing identity or history.
configuration-backup.entry: Restore matching Configuration and keyring through database/deployment backup tools.
prerequisites: Original Cluster identity, binding and supported layout are trusted.
Encrypted definitions and keys belong to the same backup; partial or unknown facts remain refused.

runtime-state.goal: Continue only from complete original durable state; otherwise require explicitly scoped recovery.
runtime-state.entry: Original runtime restart, or storage.recovery.plan/confirm for an admitted pending recovery.
prerequisites: Original CACHE identity, membership, full claim/fence and model/checkpoint closure are intact for continuation.
Loss does not mint creation rights; isolate old writers and confirm source, model, target and scope before rebuilding.

authentication.goal: Re-enter through the original account or Cloud identity without resurrecting old sessions.
authentication.entry: Original OP login or Cloud exchange after native authentication preparation.
prerequisites: Trusted CONFIG binding, completion and original account; bound CACHE is writable.
Only verified whole-empty CACHE may obtain a new scope; partial loss and conflicting identity refuse.

derived-cache.goal: Recreate derivable data from original definitions and verified artifacts after storage admission.
derived-cache.entry: Registered connector test/discovery, artifact registration or current runtime observation.
prerequisites: Original definition and exact connector artifact are available; CACHE identity is admitted.
Derived data is not saved schema history, an old observation or permission to resume a checkpoint.

legacy-preserve.goal: Retain old-layout facts without treating them as a new three-layer installation.
legacy-preserve.entry: Matching old-version backup/diagnostics; no automatic cross-layout migration.
prerequisites: Original legacy identity and matching version/backup are retained.
The current three-layer root does not admit this legacy layout.

installation-files.goal: Resume the original installation and immutable Configuration handoff.
installation-files.entry: Server installation --authorize and startup with the same installation directory.
prerequisites: OS owner, restrictive permissions, file lock and original scope remain valid.
URI, CA and database facts match; required restart and purpose-specific authorization still apply.
Original artifact remains available and matches its hash.
Local cache files do not grant runtime ownership or registry authority.

temporary-files.goal: Recreate disposable staging material for the original owned attempt.
temporary-files.entry: Owning operation creates bounded temporary files and closes/deletes them.
prerequisites: Authoritative input and original operation remain valid.
No checkpoint, keyring or ownership is recovered from temporary files.

user-files.goal: Restore user-owned settings/artifacts or recreate them with explicit user input.
user-files.entry: Existing CLI authoring/context/auth/deployment command or user backup.
prerequisites: User-selected path and permissions are valid.
Local files do not grant server roles or replace CONFIG/CACHE recovery.

build-output.goal: Rebuild metadata from the same controlled input artifacts.
prerequisites: Original input is retained.
Build output is not production ownership or a recovery checkpoint.

cache-identity.goal: Verify authentication and business preparation independently under the original binding.
cache-identity.entry: Original staged startup and native preparation under the retained CONFIG operation.
prerequisites: Original CONFIG scope and one-time preparation authority are trusted.
Authentication readiness does not authorize business creation; missing or conflicting facts remain refused.

pending-full-authority.goal: Retain authoritative generations and recognize only the exact existing explicit clear-state full rebuild; never infer a new creation or handoff right.
pending-full-authority.entry: Matching authoritative configuration backup, or the existing completed explicit clear-state full preparation for its still-current target scope.
prerequisites: Original Cluster identity, binding, complete preparation, exact operation/preparation/confirmation hash and target scope are trusted; current source/artifact/input/dependency closure is verified before and after CACHE work, without claiming a cross-domain transaction.

Generation numbers, missing rows, ordinary start/resume and a previous different operation grant no handoff authority. A retained snapshot pin always selects its original resume path; absent or incomplete pinned state cannot be reseeded.
Existing complete rebuild facts, pin and actual checkpoint govern retry after first batch; retired/deleted origins and reused Pipeline IDs cannot reauthorize an old full operation.

pending-fresh-full.goal: Preserve actual source checkpoints and referenced models while permitting one fixed fresh snapshot baseline only for an existing explicit clear-state full operation.
pending-fresh-full.entry: Original restart/recovery entries remain. The additional path is the original explicit clear-state full preparation before any replacement snapshot pin or row has been published.
prerequisites: The canonical chain, old checkpoint, membership, models and original capture preparation are complete. The old source reader and in-flight writes are safely isolated; current NODE/PIPELINE/CAPTURE fences are proved.

First publication requires no other non-detached consumer, including paused, stopped, completed or unleased references. The new exact selection must cover the entire serving/requested set. Unknown membership, unrelated override or changed input refuses.

A real existing fresh-snapshot preparation supplies exact table models and a nonempty new source cut before first row delivery. No capability or consistency proof is invented for a connector, and no PDK/JAR interface change or online DDL promise is added.

Only SRS resumeOverride has a strict pending variant: ordinary token/fromEpoch/editedAt/contentHash remain unchanged; pendingFreshFull adds formatVersion=1, origin(operationId,targetScope,preparationId,confirmationHash,sourceId), snapshotEpoch and table-to-SrsModelKey references. The hash covers the entire variant. DIRECT retains its ordinary strict decoder.

The combined BSON-encoded pending resumeOverride is at most 262144 bytes, including token, origins and model references; over-limit requests refuse before persistence. No schema body, URI or credential is copied.

One real CACHE client/session transaction competes on the original root and complete membership revisions and atomically publishes new models/context, current full-scope consumer pin, initial floors and the pending requested cut. Every new model ddlSequence must equal its observed ring largestSequence plus one; initial floor is ddlSequence minus one.

The old real checkpoint remains unchanged. The cut is a next-start request, never durableSourceRead, target ACK or snapshot completion. Stream onStart cannot checkpoint or consume this pending request.
A subsequent capture epoch reuses the fixed requested cut and exact model structure. No latest-catalog fallback, new sample cut or broad bypass of ordinary checkpoint/model validation is permitted.

Pending chain references survive origin consumer deletion and protect their models from GC. A later consumer attaches only with its own current preparation/claim; it inherits no origin execution authority. Its metadata, model and snapshot closure must be proved or it refuses.

Position editing refuses while the full request is pending. Its first real all-served checkpoint atomically records positionEditsRestricted=true in a strict SRS-only extended checkpoint variant. Every successor checkpoint monotonically preserves true. Thereafter arbitrary source tokens refuse unless exactly equal to the current actual checkpoint token; opaque tokens are never ordered or assumed model-compatible. Ordinary unchanged-model chains and DIRECT keep their original position-edit contracts.

At capture creation/reload, a typed non-authorizing CONFIG inspection of the exact canonical capture preparation/history identifies other CACHE incarnations. Trusted previous-incarnation history also requires the monotonic checkpoint marker, including ordinary onStart checkpoints before any batch. Missing or unknown required history refuses instead of defaulting to false. No auth generation is used to infer model history.

Only a real source batch with all served-table durable model frontiers can atomically publish the new checkpoint with positionEditsRestricted=true and clear the exact entire pending override. One monotonic checkpoint boolean remains; no permanent full-operation/model map or consumed history row is added.

After response loss or crash, existing snapshot pin wins; complete current-scope pin/model/floor and actual checkpoint closure are reused. Absence of a pending annex alone never grants resampling. One-sided, corrupt, missing or conflicting facts and newly changed models refuse.

Snapshot restart rereads only unfinished tables under the original pin/models/replay anchor. New sampled seams do not skip original CDC; unavailable source logs or SRS history refuse. Normal healthy unchanged-model fulls retain their original path.

Position restrictions are scoped to the same canonical capture identity. A different Pipeline using that identity, a restart or a full retry cannot lose them; Source physical identity changes remain subject to their original explicit-full and isolation contracts and do not inherit an old position request.

capture-history-position-policy.goal: Retain original capture preparation authority and conservatively identify model history outside the current CACHE incarnation without minting a new creation right.
capture-history-position-policy.entry: Existing first capture preparation or load of its exact already-issued current preparation; the additional inspection is read-only and grants no CACHE insertion.
prerequisites: Original CONFIG is complete and trusted. Inspection binds current CacheBusinessScope, canonical captureId, physical identity, SHARED_SRS chain and current preparationId; unknown or inconsistent rows refuse.

Use the existing indexed canonical capture history, explicitly excluding the current cache incarnation. At least one matching trusted previous incarnation conservatively requires restricted position editing; it does not prove a past model transition.

A negative query alone is not a fresh-history proof. Before new current-row creation the strict shared-note origin/namespace/carry consistency inspection must reject retained unaccounted facts. Existing current preparations are loaded and verified; AlreadyIssued and later consumer/writer paths cannot bypass inspection.

Current-scope preparation and CACHE incarnation replacement compete through the existing actual CONFIG version write; a late old-incarnation insertion cannot commit after scope replacement. Original first-creation rights are not reissued.

No claim of detecting simultaneous erasure of every CONFIG fact and every corroborating note is made; trusted complete CONFIG is required. Identity changes outside the canonical domain do not inherit an old execution or position request.

pending-full-input-proof.entry: A newly confirmed explicit clear-state full writes strict stateRebuild formatVersion 2 in the original CONFIG begin transaction, after original intent, input and complete dependency verification; completedFull recognizes only the same still-current COMPLETE target.
prerequisites: Strict version 2 is exactly the existing version 1 stateRebuild fields plus inputClosureHash, with the existing result added only on completion. inputClosureHash is the canonical hash of the exact existing encoded PipelinePreparationInputs and lexically sorted complete dependencyHashes map from the original confirmed request. It is written and retained with the original operation, preparation, scopes and confirmationHash in the same CONFIG transaction/CAS.

At first model handoff and its subsequent CONFIG guard, recompute the exact current input/dependency digest, verify all current referenced resources and canonical hashes, compare the original fixed digest, and require the original ACTIVE target, COMPLETE preparation, operation and strict completed result. Dependency IDs, hashes, input selections and direct-channel identities all contribute; equality grants no extra scope.

Existing version 1 pending/completed facts keep their strict original shapes and ordinary replay behavior. They cannot authorize this new model handoff; no migration, inference, missing-proof backfill or current-only substitute is allowed. A new explicit clear-state full is required to create version 2 proof.

Completed-full handles are minted and revalidated by the original CONFIG adapter; a caller-supplied origin/hash or arbitrary SPI implementation is not proof. CACHE separately checks the exact original rebuild marker, target and claims in its existing transaction, while CONFIG checks remain outside that transaction before and after it. There is no cross-domain atomicity promise.

All previously reviewed pending-full pin-first retry, model/cut, membership, size and monotonic position-edit restriction contracts remain unchanged. A retired/deleted origin, reused Pipeline ID, later full or changed preparation cannot reuse a prior proof.

Additional entry: exact single shared SRS impact preflight and explicit confirmation, original writer drain, guarded namespace replacement and per-Pipeline explicit clear-state full.

Only a separately and explicitly confirmed single canonical shared SRS recovery may replace its current physical chain namespace. Its original configuration binding, capture birth/preparation and CAPTURE claim, complete root/consumer relations and progress controls must be trustworthy; payload loss never grants ordinary first creation. Unknown control, conflicting identity or unproved prior source/target drain refuses.

The typed control-only preflight binds the exact old effective preparation, CAPTURE fence, root/control digest, complete non-detached consumer keys and revisions, original Pipeline scopes and complete current authoring dependency hashes. Paused, stopped, completed and unleased retained relations are included. Missing model/event bodies cannot be replaced with latest, guessed bounds, fake events, source checkpoints, ACKs or trims.

CONFIG storage_recovery.pendingRecovery has an additional strict formatVersion 2 SHARED_SRS variant for exactly one canonical/current physical chain. It retains the operation, original scope, immutable confirmation, actual affected IDs and a bounded sharedSrs control annex; its combined BSON is at most 262144 bytes. Existing PIPELINE/CLUSTER version 1 variants retain their shapes and behavior.

CONFIG capture_preparations retains its immutable original birth. A strict version 2 optional currentRecovery annex fixes formatVersion 1, operationId, planHash, previousPhysicalChain, previousPreparationId, physicalChain and phase RESERVED or READY. The operation UUID is the new preparationId; the replacement physical ID deterministically hashes the exact business scope, canonical chain and operation UUID. A single flat predecessor is kept, never a recursive lineage. Retries reuse the same IDs.

CONFIG operator_generations has an optional sharedRecovery annex exactly formatVersion 1, operationId and originalScope. It is only a scope-bound requirement for explicit clear-state full, never capture creation or business authority. The joint start transaction installs or replaces it only on an exact ACTIVE, COMPLETE-prepared current scope with no in-flight full/retirement, leaves original generation, operationId, preparation and stateRebuild intact, and writes STOPPED intents for the actual affected scopes. No unrelated Pipeline is changed.

Ordinary START/resume, intent CAS and execution preparation consume the scope gate. STOPPED controls and explicitly requested purge/full remain operable. Only the winning existing full completion transaction, proving the exact original scope and marker, removes it while completing the original rebuild and purge consumption; completed-result replay cannot remove a newer marker. Verified retirement/recreate handles the old scope marker without copying it to a new generation.

CONFIG reservation and guarded publication use the existing configuration version contention point. New canonical capture/attach/full admission refuses RESERVED mappings, including every Pipeline whose full needs that mapping; previously issued operations still compete on the actual CACHE root. CONFIG proof runs before and after CACHE work, never inside a CACHE transaction or under a claim of cross-database atomicity.

A dedicated opaque recovery handle binds the original CONFIG reservation and exact original CACHE control view. One actual CACHE client/session transaction proves the current NODE and ended original CAPTURE/affected Pipeline tenures, safely advances the known canonical CAPTURE counters/annex, expires only exact old Pipeline tenures while preserving their private claims/state/notes, detaches the complete old shared relations and removes their corresponding offsets, retires the old root and creates the entirely empty replacement physical root. A normal AlreadyIssued or caller-built SPI value supplies no such authority.

The old srs_chains root has a strict version 2 recoveryControl annex exactly formatVersion 1, operationId, planHash, replacementChain, phase CANCELLED or RETIRED, and controlHash. The digest binds the exact typed poststage root/relationship controls and detached-cursor absence, excluding itself. Every ordinary old-domain load/write/model/log/epoch/consumer path refuses before reading lost payload. Dedicated typed retired control reads reprove exact relations, scopes, counts/revisions and absent offsets; they cannot blindly skip an old root or require all old roots to name the latest Pipeline gate operation.

RETIRED plus the exact new physical root and CAPTURE annex is the joint CACHE commit receipt. If application is absent or unknown, cancellation must first arbitrate with it in the same CACHE root CAS, prove the old effective annex and complete emptiness of the replacement namespace, and record CANCELLED for the exact old operation/plan. A late application cannot pass a winning cancellation; a winning application is completed, never rolled back. Unknown evidence keeps the reservation closed.

Only the exact CACHE CANCELLED receipt permits a protected same-operation RUNNING to PLANNED preflight transition. RESERVED and all prior STOPPED/scope gates stay; physical/preparation IDs do not change. The actual current closure and configuration version produce a new planHash/controlRevision and require new explicit human confirmation. A new reservation attempt CAS consumes the exact prior cancellation. The generic plan/transition entry cannot confer this permission, and scope expansion never reuses an old operational isolation confirmation.

A shared-specific completion guard proves the original RUNNING reservation and exact physical/preparation/CACHE receipt, then atomically publishes mapping READY and joint COMPLETE. It does not reinterpret later authoring or run the generic current-definition completion check. Original affected scopes remain stopped/gated; subsequent per-Pipeline full separately confirms all current source/selection/dependency/target/retirement inputs. Existing-state continuation is never silently converted into full.

All native writers, planners and readers resolve one trusted effective physical chain and use matching ring/model/consumer keys. The canonical CAPTURE read identity and the original canonical shared notes namespace remain stable; the new physical identity must never create empty replacement necessary notes or change their original connector/config/artifact origin. Position-edit restrictions follow canonical historical identity across replacement namespaces.

For A reading S1 and S2, B reading S1 and C reading S2, only damaged S1 and actual A/B are jointly recovered. A later explicit full may detach A from healthy S2 and update ordinary membership counters, but cannot reset S2 epoch/checkpoint/models or C authorization/cursor/execution. No running, stopped or completed Pipeline is automatically started.

No new collection, protocol lease, event history, stored model body or credential is added by this control contract. CONFIG retains one current bounded plan, one current mapping plus flat predecessor per canonical capture, and one scope gate per affected Pipeline. Each actual recovery leaves an old quarantined physical namespace and retirement marker; precise final destruction is outside this entry, required identity cannot be discarded for a budget and insufficient capacity refuses. Existing ordinary model/log/retention and pending-full budgets and validation remain.

The recovery CAPTURE claim annex is exactly formatVersion 2, original (the complete immutable version 1 birth row), physicalChain and preparationId. The preparationId equals the fixed operation UUID. Its CONFIG currentRecovery keeps only previousPhysicalChain and previousPreparationId as a flat predecessor; canonical predecessor coordinates must match the immutable birth. The Pipeline sharedRecovery marker never changes original operationId/preparation/stateRebuild and is consumed only by the winning exact old-scope full completion, never by replay or an unrelated generation.
